summary: Excellent architectural refactor. New workflow-manifest-schema.ts centralizes all manifest parsing, Zod validation, and type inference. AgentRole derived via z.infer eliminates the previously manual union maintenance. ManifestSchema.parse() at module-load produces a clear ZodError on malformed manifest — fail-fast behavior correctly tested. constants.ts, enums.ts, and pipeline-maps.ts all migrated to import workflowManifest from the singleton, eliminating 3 separate createRequire usages. One remaining raw createRequire in workflow-helpers.ts is correctly flagged as follow-on debt (outside WP scope). ManifestSchema.roles.length(9) + RoleSchema.name: AgentRoleEnum provides a two-layer consistency guard between manifest data and TypeScript types. 1472/1472 tests pass, build clean.

comments.note: AgentRoleEnum in workflow-manifest-schema.ts is the one construct that is NOT derived from the manifest — the 9 string literals must match manual updates when roles change. This is architecturally correct for Zod enums (TypeScript needs string literal types), and the ManifestSchema.roles.length(9) + name: AgentRoleEnum guards ensure any divergence causes a startup-time ZodError. Worth documenting explicitly: when adding a new agent role, both workflow-manifest.json AND AgentRoleEnum + .length(9) must be updated atomically. Non-blocking, informational.

workflow-helpers.ts (lines 11, 20) still imports the manifest via createRequire + raw cast, bypassing the new Zod-validated singleton. This means workflow-helpers.ts gets loosely-typed manifest access compared to all other consumers. Correctly identified as follow-on debt in both implementation and QA pipelines. Future WP should migrate it to import { workflowManifest } from '../schema/workflow-manifest-schema.js'.
